newsitem.title: UK: British Greens launch manifesto - again.
newsitem.headline: British Greens launch manifesto - again.

text.p: Britain's environmentalist Green Party launched its election manifesto for the second time on Friday because the media all but ignored it the first time round.

Party spokesman David Taylor said only one national newspaper had bothered to cover the party's blueprint for a green alternative to the "grey" policies of Britain's mainstream parties when it was first unveiled last month, before the official start of the election campaign.
"We will continue launching this throughout the campaign to ensure that the Green Party gets fair coverage," Taylor told a news conference.
The Greens are fielding 90 candidates in the May 1 general election, compared with the 255 they put up in 1992.
They have no members of parliament and the highest level of support they received in a general election was 3.4 percent. But they have more than 100 local councillors.

The Greens complained that their policies are often hijacked by the mainstream parties and Green voters are put off because Britain's first-past-the-post electoral system means the party is unlikely to enter parliament.
Green support in Britain peaked in 1989, when the party won 15 percent of the vote in elections to the European Parliament.
If Britain had Proportional Representation, as the Greens want, the party would have had 12 Members of the European Parliament, but instead it got none.

Outlining the Greens' policies, Taylor said the party wanted to introduce a new regime of economic indicators to measure "real wealth" together with community banks, green taxes and measures to cut road traffic.
Other policies included powers to fill empty houses, an end to factory farming, possible British withdrawal from the European Union, British nuclear disarmament and writing off Third World debt.
"Green politics is not a single issue," said Taylor. "It is a comprehensive political philosophy."
